items.area: R1 — cleanup never deletes a pinned image
items.description: registry-cleanup must never delete an image a deploy repo pins (R1), as ruled without reading what is deployed: the would-delete list of the dry-run the test phase starts by hand from the unsuspended CronJob — tag deletions and garbage collection alike — holds no tag and no digest that any deploy repo pins for an image from the estate's registry.
items.rationale: Needs the hand-started dry-run Job from the unsuspended RegistryDeploy CronJob (Ordering constraints step 5), which needs DockerImages (step 3), the keycloak build (step 4) and RegistryDeploy (step 5) pushed first. This test-phase run stopped after step 2 (see close-out 'Outstanding actions'): the dispatch's deterministic facts pre-authorise pushing and rolling dev under the devlock and state prd stays operator-gated, which conflicts with plan.md's Ruling R1-Q2 (the operator's 2026-09-26 authorisation for the test phase to push the whole chain, prd rollouts included, unattended). Command for whoever runs the rest: see the Outstanding actions entry for the exact sequence.
evidence: verification.json V01 needs the run this entry describes

items.area: R1 — the pause is lifted (Ruling D1)
items.description: The registry-cleanup CronJob is no longer suspended and runs nightly in dry-run: the RegistryDeploy chart carries a dry-run setting, turned on, and a run logs what it would delete — garbage collection with `--delete-untagged` included — and deletes nothing. Today the CronJob carries `suspend: true` (RegistryDeploy `chart/templates/registry-cleanup-cronjob.yaml:7-10`) and a dry run skips garbage collection (DockerImages `registry-cleanup/app/main.py:467`; GC at `:143-148`).
items.rationale: Code is shipped and ready: RegistryDeploy chart/templates/registry-cleanup-cronjob.yaml wires env DRY_RUN from .Values.registryCleanup.dryRun with a `fail` guard if not bool, the suspend field and its comment are gone from the template, and config/prd/values.yaml sets registryCleanup.dryRun: true (read 2026-09-29, RegistryDeploy commit dca461d, not yet pushed). Live, the CronJob is still `suspend: true` on image registry-cleanup:2548 (read 2026-09-29: `kubectl get cronjob registry-cleanup -n registry-prd` -> SUSPEND=True, last schedule 4d6h ago) because RegistryDeploy was not pushed this round — see V01's rationale and the Outstanding actions close-out entry for why and the remaining command sequence.
evidence: live: kubectl get cronjob registry-cleanup -n registry-prd, read-only, 2026-09-29

items.rationale: Depends on V01/V02's live unsuspend + hand-started Job, not reached this round. See close-out Outstanding actions for the remaining command sequence.

items.rationale: The Operator Action card is filed only after V01/V03's would-delete list exists (Ruling D1: "never before"); that list does not exist yet, so no card was filed this round. See close-out Outstanding actions.

items.description: Deploy repos pin tags, never digests, for images from the estate's registry: every such pin is a per-build tag, which is never rebuilt, so it always points at the same image. KeycloakDeploy's two stages — the only deploy-repo digest pins of an in-registry image (`config/dev/values.yaml:21`, `config/prd/values.yaml:22`, `@sha256:45ae4959…`) — pin a per-build tag.
items.rationale: Needs the live keycloak build (Ordering constraints step 4), which needs DockerImages pushed first (step 3). Not reached this round — see close-out Outstanding actions for why (the authorisation-scope conflict) and the remaining command sequence. Every other estate image was already tag-pinned per the plan's grounding; KeycloakDeploy's two stages are the one remaining digest pin (`@sha256:45ae4959…`), unchanged as of this run.
evidence: plan.md grounding, 'Pin freshness, measured against the live registry'

items.description: The "digest the release runs" comment that the migration left in every deploy repo is corrected in each repo that carried it, RegistryDeploy's (`config/prd/values.yaml:26-27`) and KeycloakDeploy's two copies included. The corrected text is written once, in RegistryDeploy, and every other copy is replaced by that exact string (Ruling R1-Q3); it stays true in a file that still pins an upstream image by digest (ANS-139). The five repos with a different migration header change only where they claim digests, and each such change is listed in the close-out.
items.rationale: The comment sweep (Ordering constraints step 6) runs after steps 3-5; not reached this round. RegistryDeploy's own corrected comment (the source string) is already committed and verified in place at config/prd/values.yaml:31-33 (read 2026-09-29), but not yet pushed, and the sweep into the other ~40 deploy repos has not started. items.description: argo-cd D53 is amended: deploy repos pin tags only, never digests, for images from the estate's registry (`AnsibleSpecs/argo-cd/decisions.md:836-848` never mentions digests today).
items.rationale: AnsibleSpecs argo-cd/decisions.md:854-870 carries the dated amendment (2026-09-26, operator "Go", slice 031/ANS-125): a pin names a per-build tag, never a digest, for registry:5000 images; a matrix build's per-build tag is written wherever a pin list exists (today only keycloak's); Argo CD's relay pin is written by relay builds, leaving argocd-prd out of sync for the operator; upstream digest pins stay ANS-139's. No existing D53 sentence changed. Committed (AnsibleSpecs 14308f1, P9) and confirmed by direct read 2026-09-29.

items.description: Every matrix build pushes `<tag>-<build>` next to the named tag, and the pin stage writes the per-build tag wherever a `deploy-pins.json` exists, which today is only Keycloak; the other seven keep pulling their named tag. Today a matrix build pushes its named tag only and is left out of the pin stage (DockerImages `Jenkinsfile:120-121`).
items.rationale: Verified by independent code read (sub-agent, 2026-09-29) against DockerImages dd8e7f4: Jenkinsfile:131 computes `<tag>-<build>` for a matrix build; the matrix branch (:158-165) pushes it next to the named tag and passes the named tag as `trackingTag`; `collectPins` (:39-55) now iterates every built image's tag map (matrix included), where the pre-P6 code explicitly excluded matrix images. kube-coder-tunnel-reclaim/deploy-pins.json is new, naming KubeCoderDeploy's two stage files at images.tunnelReclaim; webhook-relay/deploy-pins.json gained ArgoCDDeploy's config/prd/values.yaml at relay.image next to FieldnotesDeploy's entry. Of the 7 build-matrix.json files, the 6 non-keycloak ones have no deploy-pins.json, so they keep pulling their named tag.

items.area: R3 — Keycloak runs a per-build tag
items.description: Keycloak's dev and prd stages run the per-build tag (`26.7.3-postgres-health-ispn-<build>`) a keycloak build wrote into KeycloakDeploy, Synced and Healthy, before the dry-run CronJob was unsuspended.
items.rationale: Needs the live keycloak build (Ordering constraints step 4); not reached this round. See close-out Outstanding actions.

items.description: The image's label, not the tag's name, decides what is build history: registry-cleanup treats a tag as tracking only if its name equals the `org.webathome.poller.tracking-tag` label on the image it points to, deletes only tags in that label's build series (Ruling D2: `latest` owns the bare build numbers, `dev-latest` owns `dev-<n>`, a matrix label such as `26.7.3-postgres-health-ispn` owns `26.7.3-postgres-health-ispn-<n>`), and keeps every other tag without counting it toward the keep-newest cap — unlabelled tags and promoted `prd-<n>` copies included. `node-24` and `jdk-21` are no longer treated as build 24 and build 21 (today's regex: `registry-cleanup/app/main.py:29`).
items.rationale: Verified by independent code read (sub-agent, 2026-09-29) against DockerImages 9a11863: registry-cleanup/app/main.py's old regex machinery (_VERSIONED, is_versioned, _family_and_number) is gone (grep clean); classification is build_number(tag, label) reading the image's tracking-tag label (main.py:36,49-64), applied per-tag in cleanup_repo (:266-275); --max-per-series cap (:296-305) and per-series floor (:320-332) match D2/R1-A1; the shared-digest guard (:354-380, fails closed) and GC with --delete-untagged and --dry-run (:132-171) both still exist.

items.description: `kaniko2` takes an explicit `trackingTag:` with the current derivation from tag shapes as the default; a build that pushes only a build number is labelled so that number falls in the label's series; a matrix build's named tag plus its per-build tag is accepted, where today the check refuses it (JenkinsPipelineUtils `vars/helmCharts.groovy:144-165`).
items.rationale: Verified by independent code read (sub-agent, 2026-09-29) against JenkinsPipelineUtils 276beff: vars/helmCharts.groovy:108 passes an explicit trackingTag into resolveTrackingTag (:158); without one, a lone bare-number destination is labelled `latest` (:162-163), otherwise the one destination whose build series (inBuildSeries, :190-198) covers every other is the label (:165) — which accepts a matrix build's `<tag>`+`<tag>-<build>` pair, refused by the old code (confirmed by diff: the pre-P1 check only handled 1-2 destinations via a `^(.*-)?latest$` regex). Lines 173-183 refuse a bare-number label and any destination outside the label's series. New tests/src/test/java/.../TrackingTagTest.java, 23/23 passing (surefire report read). Gate log phases/P1/gate_r1.log confirms the whole Maven suite green.

items.description: The version-poller classifies tags by the same label rule, so its fallback to the label (`version-poller/app/poller.py:125-132`, `:220-238`) stops being a fallback, and neither the poller nor registry-cleanup carries the tag-shape regex any more (`version-poller/app/tagging.py:20`, `registry-cleanup/app/main.py:29`).
items.rationale: Verified by independent code read (sub-agent, 2026-09-29) against DockerImages 1a69ff9: version-poller/app/tagging.py's build_number (tagging.py:21-37) mirrors cleanup's exactly, with no regex/is_versioned/fallback remnants (grep clean); poller.py:139-151 classifies each tag directly by label (tag==label -> tracking; build_number match -> history/ignored; self-labelled bare number -> explicit leftover skip); no _recover_self_tracking_tags exists anywhere in the repo.

items.area: R4 — no rebuilds through leftover labels
items.description: Moving the poller to the label rule starts no rebuild through a legacy build-number tag whose label names the tag itself (live example: `dhcpapp:35`, labelled `35`, pipeline `DHCP/DHCPApp`, rebuild-at 2026-07-18); the only new rebuild targets are tracking tags the name heuristic misread, such as `node-24`.
items.rationale: Verified by independent read (sub-agent, 2026-09-29) of the already-executed live dry-run logs from P5 (phases/P5/poller-dryrun-week-{old,new}.log): dhcpapp-validation and ssegateway-validation log 'no tracking tag' identically on every one of 9 daily polls, old and new code alike. The P4 cleanup dry-run (phases/P4/cleanup-dryrun-new.log) confirms the leftover shape: dhcpapp holds tracking tags {35, latest} and ssegateway-validation holds 8 self-labelled bare numbers (48-52,54-56) — matching the claimed 9 leftovers exactly. DHCP/DHCPApp does fire in both logs, but only via its legitimate `latest` tag, never through `35`. New unit test test_leftover_self_labelled_build_numbers_never_trigger (version-poller/tests/test_timer_poller.py:245-264) reproduces the scenario synthetically.

items.description: DockerImages' `docs/registry-management/version-poller-redesign.md` §4 ("Tag scheme (enforced by `kaniko2`)" and the mirror classifier, `:142-165`) and §8's keep/delete rules state the label rule, per the triage ruling that overruled the one-tag scheme.
items.rationale: Verified by independent read (sub-agent, 2026-09-29) against DockerImages docs/registry-management/version-poller-redesign.md at 2748608/18dadc8: §4 heading is now 'Tag scheme and build series (enforced by kaniko2)' with the shared classifier (tracking / build history / promoted copy / unlabelled / self-labelled bare-number leftover) at :172-190, replacing the old regex scheme and 'No exotic schemes' language (confirmed absent by diff against the pre-P8 version). §8's keep/delete rules (:457-524) are fully label-based; §11's defaults table reads '--max-per-series'. A full-file grep found no leftover old-scheme material.

items.area: Ruling R1-A1 — every label series keeps its newest build
items.description: registry-cleanup's floor keeps the newest build of each label series whether or not the label's own tag exists in the repo, so an old self-labelled bare number (live example: `ssegateway-validation:56`, labelled `56`, built 2026-09-24) counting as a tracking tag cannot switch the floor off. Today the floor fires only in a repo with no tracking tag (`registry-cleanup/app/main.py:319`).
items.rationale: Verified by independent code read (sub-agent, 2026-09-29): main.py:320-322 pops the series' highest build number out of the delete set unconditionally, keyed by the label string itself -- never requiring a tag actually named after that label to exist. Confirmed by test_floor_keeps_the_newest_build_without_the_label_tag (test_cleanup.py:222-227) and, matching the live ssegateway-validation shape exactly, test_floor_holds_next_to_a_self_labelled_bare_number (test_cleanup.py:230-237): a self-labelled '56' tracking tag sits beside a labelless `latest` series (57,58,59), and 59 is still kept by the floor.
